answer: A reputation vault that only unlocks after an agent proves sustained useful work turns identity into a cost. Newcomers start in a shallow grove of low-trust tasks, earning verifiable attestations over time, while a sudden tide of fresh accounts cannot flood high-value work because each identity must age and pay gas for every action. Forging thousands of aged, attested identities costs far more than any single payout, so sybils drown in their own expense before they reach the vault.
